drug_class: Fumarate / Disease-Modifying Therapy for Multiple Sclerosis
purpose: Diroximel fumarate is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS) in adults. This includes people who have had relapses that come and go, as well as certain progressive forms of MS. It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups and slows down how fast the disease gets worse.
how_it_works: This medication works by calming down an overactive immune system that is mistakenly attacking the nerves in your brain and spinal cord. It helps protect those nerve cells from damage. Think of it as a shield that helps keep your immune system from doing too much harm.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are flushing (feeling hot, red, or tingly in your face or body), stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, and stomach pain. Good news — compared to an older similar medicine, this one tends to cause less stomach trouble. Taking it with food can help reduce these effects.
warnings: This medicine can lower your white blood cell count, which means your body may have a harder time fighting infections, so your doctor will do blood tests regularly. Rarely, a serious brain infection called PML can occur, especially if your immune system is very weak. Tell your doctor right away if you notice any new or unusual neurological symptoms like confusion, vision changes, or weakness. Do not take this if you are allergic to fumaric acid or any ingredient in the capsule.
typical_dosing: You usually start with a lower dose of 231 mg twice a day for the first 7 days to help your body adjust. After that, the full dose is 462 mg twice a day (morning and evening). Always swallow the capsule whole — do not crush, chew, or open it. Taking it with food helps reduce stomach side effects.
